entries.english:
Political correspondence of the Hessian prime minister Reinhard von Dalwigk.

Contains: Emil Palleske, actor and Schiller biographer (2 items), 1862; Karl Friedrich Parcus, district assessor in Worms (situation in 1850) and district councillor in Bingen (von Harter and his mistress in Ingelheim) (4), 1850/57, including a letter from Privy Councillor Schmitt at Mainz, 1856; Dr. August Parcus, director of the Bank for Trade and Industry, Darmstadt (2), 1858; Heinrich Pauli, justice of the peace in Osthofen (1), 1868; Franz Freiherr von Paumgarten, Imperial and Royal field marshal lieutenant, deputy governor of Mainz fortress (6), 1856/63; Wilhelm Reichsgraf von Perponcher-Sedlintzky [son of the Royal Netherlands infantry general and Countess A. von Reede-Ginckel], Prussian envoy in Darmstadt (22), 1855/57 and undated; Johann Pfannebecker, district councillor in Worms (7), 1848, 1854/68; von Pfeufer, Bavarian royal government president, Speyer (1), 1867; Franz von Pfeuffer, Baden grand-ducal envoy in Darmstadt (1), 1870; Ludwig Freiherr von der Pfordten, Bavarian royal state minister (38), 1858/73, with two draft replies by Dalwigk (1854, 1866); Caroline Pierson, née von Leonhardt (concerning composer Hugo Pierson) (2), 1863, including a letter from English federal envoy Sir A. Malet; Friedrich Pietsch, government councillor in Giessen (1), 1850; E. Th. Prof. Dr. Pistor, grammar-school teacher in Darmstadt (1), 1865; Carl Pistor, municipal judge in Darmstadt (‘Pistor’s examination’), cousin of Fr. O. von Müller (1), 1860; Dr. Johann Baptist Pitschaft, president of the Higher Court in Mainz (4), 1851/54; Aloys Carl Ploch, district judge in Giessen (1), 1858; Mélanie Gräfin von Pourtalès-Gorgier [daughter of Baron Alfred Renouard de Bussierre at Ruprechtsau near Strasbourg], wife of Count Edmond (1), 18 April 1871 concerning Dalwigk’s departure, including a letter from her husband in 1873; Arthur Graf von Pourtalès-Gorgier, French imperial attaché in Darmstadt (1), 1868; Siegmund Freiherr von Pranckh, Bavarian royal war minister (2), 1870; Wilhelm der Ältere, Prince von Preußen [1783/1851] (2), 1846, 1849; Marianne, Princess von Preußen, née Princess of the Netherlands, wife of Prince Albrecht der Ältere (1), 1943, with a draft reply by Dalwigk; Anton Freiherr von Prokesch-Osten, Imperial and Royal federal presidential envoy in Frankfurt (6), 1853, 1865; M. J. Auguste Baron de Pron, imperial prefect of Lower Alsace in Strasbourg (4), 1866/69, including a draft reply by Dalwigk; Hermann Freiherr von Nordeck zur Rabenau, deputy order chancellor, later chief chamberlain (1), 1852; Don Manuel Rancés y Villanueva, Spanish royal envoy for Hesse (3), 1860/62; Otto Graf zu Rantzau-Breitenburg, Baden grand-ducal legation councillor (1), 1871; Dr. Juan Antonio de Rascon, Spanish royal envoy to the Federal Diet and for Hesse, later in Berlin (3), 1863/1870; Dr. Carl Ferdinand Reatz, court-court advocate in Giessen, private lecturer in law (2), 1861; Johann Bernhard Graf von Rechberg und Rothenlöwen, federal presidential envoy, later Imperial and Royal foreign minister (26), 1855/63, including one telegram each from Prince Alexander von Hessen to Dalwigk and to the Tsarina, 1857; Freiherr von Reden, Vienna (1), 1857; Heinrich Graf von Redern, Prussian royal envoy in Turin and Dresden, formerly chargé d’affaires in Darmstadt (5), 1855/62 and undated; Georg Reich, teacher at the secondary school in Offenbach, later pastor in Reichelsheim/Odenwald (1850), including no. 77 of the Politisch-kirchliche Blätter published in Darmstadt; Reichert, mayor in Mettenheim (1), 1850; Ludwig Freiherr von Reinhard, Württemberg royal envoy to the Federal Diet and for Hesse (12), 1857/65; Gustave Comte de Reiset, French imperial envoy in Darmstadt, later Hanover (46), 1860/66 and undated, including a 1860 letter from Count Alfred de Salignac-Fénélon, French imperial federal envoy, to de Reiset; August Reuning, mayor in Nidda (2), 1865/69; Franz Freiherr von Reyer, Imperial and Royal legation councillor and chargé d’affaires in Darmstadt [son-in-law of Baron Prokesch-Osten, see above] (5), 1863/64; Freiherr von und zu Rhein, Bavarian royal government president in Würzburg (2), 1860, with duplicated memoranda and consultation programs for an economic conference, 1860; Carl Freiherr von Ricou, ministerial councillor and chief steward to Prince Carl von Hessen (25), 1848/71, including two petitions to the Grand Duke, 1850; Ludwig Freiherr von Riedesel zu Eisenbach, Ludwigseck line (1), 1851; Georg Freiherr von Riedesel zu Eisenbach, Altenburg line (1), 1865; Franz Joseph von Rieffel, ministerial councillor in Darmstadt (4), 1852/55; Ad. Rigant, Weißenburg, Alsace (1), 1866?; Napoleon de Ring, French imperial chargé d’affaires in Berlin (1), 1866?; Hugo Prof. Dr. von Ritgen, privy building councillor and professor in Giessen (1), 1860; Friedrich Ludwig Ritter, pastor in Planig (20), 1851/61; Wilhelm Friedrich Rochussen, legation secretary at the Royal Netherlands embassy in Paris (1), 1859; Maximilian Freiherr von Rodenstein-Überbruck, ministerial councillor in Darmstadt (3), 1868/77; Ludwig Freiherr Röder von Diersburg, district administrator in Biedenkopf (1), 1863; Prof. Dr. K. Röder, Heidelberg (2), 1868; von Rosenberg, Prussian royal legation secretary at the Federal Diet [probably the later envoy in Stockholm and Stuttgart, Adalbert Freiherr von Rosenberg] (3), 1850/52; Carl Rosenstiel, Imperial and Royal navy ensign; Meyer Carl Freiherr von Rothschild, banker in Frankfurt and Bavarian royal consul-general (18), 1854/69, with a draft reply by Dalwigk; Wilhelm Carl Freiherr von Rothschild, banker and Imperial and Royal consul-general in Frankfurt (1), 1866; Rycroft (1), undated; Rzikowski von Dobrschitz, Imperial and Royal colonel and military plenipotentiary at the Federal Diet (3), 1857/59.
